title: Place and direction
intro: Read plate 2 for the prepositions. These are the adverbs that go with them. Spanish has a three-way distance system where English has two: aquí here, ahí there near you, allí there further off.

entries.note: acá is commoner in Latin America and suggests movement towards the speaker: ven acá.

ex.es: Ponlo aquí, junto a la ventana.
ex.en: Put it here, next to the window.

entries.note: A genuine three-way scale: ahí is near the listener, allí further, allá vaguer and further still.

ex.en: There it is, in your hand.
My grandmother lived there.

ex.es: Allá en el norte hace frío.
ex.en: Up there in the north it's cold.
The children are upstairs.
I'll wait for you downstairs.

entries.note: Spain prefers dentro and fuera; Latin America adds the a-.

ex.en: Let's go inside, it's cold.
The dog sleeps outside.
Carry straight on for two streets.

ex.es: Se quedó atrás con las maletas.
ex.en: He stayed behind with the suitcases.

entries.note: a la derecha, a la izquierda. derecho as an adverb means straight ahead, so a la derecha and derecho are different instructions.

ex.es: Gira a la derecha en la esquina.
ex.en: Turn right at the corner.

ex.es: El baño está a la izquierda.
ex.en: The bathroom is on the left.

entries.en: straight ahead; a right, the law
entries.note: sigue derecho is carry straight on. los derechos humanos are human rights; estudiar derecho is to study law.

ex.en: Go straight on to the traffic lights.
You have a right to know.

entries.note: Both take de before a noun: cerca de la escuela.

ex.en: I live near the market.
It's very far from here.

entries.note: Not capitalised. al norte de means to the north of.

ex.es: Viven en el norte del país.
ex.en: They live in the north of the country.

ex.es: El clima del sur es más cálido.
ex.en: The climate in the south is warmer.

ex.es: El sol sale por el este.
ex.en: The sun rises in the east.

ex.es: La costa oeste es más lluviosa.
ex.en: The west coast is rainier.

ex.es: Ponlo en el centro de la mesa.
ex.en: Put it in the centre of the table.
I work downtown.

entries.note: al lado de is next to — see plate 2. por un lado ... por otro lado is on the one hand ... on the other.

ex.en: Sit next to me.

entries.note: en lugar de means instead of; tener lugar to take place.

ex.es: Es mi lugar favorito de la ciudad.
ex.en: It's my favourite place in the city.

entries.note: A room has rincones; streets meet at an esquina.

ex.es: La planta está en el rincón.
ex.en: The plant is in the corner.
I'll wait for you on the corner.

entries.note: Used of rivers and the sea. el borde is any edge.

ex.es: No te pares en el borde.
ex.en: Don't stand on the edge.

ex.es: Caminamos por la orilla del río.
ex.en: We walked along the river bank.

entries.note: alrededor de before a noun, and also used for approximately: alrededor de veinte.

ex.es: Miró alrededor pero no vio nada.
ex.en: He looked around but saw nothing.

entries.note: For an interruption Spanish also says en pleno: en plena reunión.

ex.es: Se paró en medio de la calle.
ex.en: He stopped in the middle of the street.

entries.note: Distinct from delante de, which is simply in front of. enfrente implies facing across a gap.

ex.es: La farmacia está enfrente del banco.
ex.en: The pharmacy is opposite the bank.
He walked towards the door.
They arrived around ten.

entries.note: en ninguna parte is nowhere, and needs no before the verb.

ex.en: You can sit anywhere.
There's rubbish everywhere.
